records.issue_text: EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the requesting user's credentials) instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong or empty credential set and external calendar/video events are silently not updated
records.rationale: The diff shows `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` in addGuests.handler.ts, even though the booking is fetched with its own `user` (organizer) and the permission check allows any attendee of the booking to invoke the mutation. Using the requesting user's credentials to update the organizer's external calendar event is plausibly the wrong or empty credential set, so `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` may silently fail for non-organizer callers. This is a genuine correctness concern in newly added code.

records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedup compares `guest === attendee.email` case-sensitively, so adding Foo@Bar.com when foo@bar.com already exists creates a duplicate attendee and duplicate invite
records.rationale: The diff's dedup logic `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` performs a strict case-sensitive equality, so 'Foo@Bar.com' would not match an existing 'foo@bar.com' attendee and would be inserted via createMany, creating a duplicate attendee and duplicate email/invite. Email addresses are case-insensitive in the local-part-delivery sense and elsewhere the code lowercases (e.g., BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased for comparison but guests are not), confirming the inconsistency.

records.issue_text: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `message` is always a non-empty template string, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and exposing raw error codes to users
records.rationale: The diff shows `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` followed by `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"))`. The template literal is always a non-empty string (even worst case yields 'undefined: ...' which is truthy), so the fallback is dead code and users see raw error codes like 'BAD_REQUEST: ...' in the toast. This is a real, verifiable minor defect introduced by the new dialog code.

records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard, throwing on bookings with no attendees and failing the entire email send
records.rationale: The only caller is addGuestsHandler, which constructs evt.attendees from bookingAttendees.attendees after `attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails } }` — and it already throws `BAD_REQUEST` if `uniqueGuests.length === 0`. So by the time sendAddGuestsEmails → OrganizerAddGuestsEmail runs, `this.calEvent.attendees[0]` is guaranteed to exist (at minimum the newly added guests). The 'bookings with no attendees' crash scenario is unreachable via this diff's code path.

records.issue_text: Read (findFirst for existing attendees) and write (booking.update + createMany) are not in a transaction and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent add-guest requests with the same email both insert
records.rationale: The diff shows addGuests.handler.ts doing a prisma.booking.findFirst to read existing attendees, then a separate prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany, with no transaction or upsert. Concurrent requests with overlapping guest emails could both pass the uniqueness filter and insert duplicates. The claim that no unique constraint exists on (bookingId, email) cannot be verified from the diff (no schema shown), so confidence is reduced, but the non-transactional read-then-write mechanism is directly visible.
